sub_module: Canvas Rendering, Real-Time Pitch Tracking & Gamified Vocal Learning Engine
description: High-engagement, playful interactive learning suite for Carnatic Gamakas and Swara mastery. Blends video-game-style flight mechanics ('Nāda Vāhana') and ear-training arcade games with strict 22-Śruti musicological rigor, microtonal boundary guardrails, and real-time DSP pitch tracking.

canonical_definition.sanskrit: स्वरस्य कम्पनं गमको श्रोतृचित्तसुखावहः (Swarasya kampo Gamakaha srotrchitta sukhavahah)
canonical_definition.translation: The oscillation or graceful embellishment of a swara that produces a pleasing, soothing effect on the listener.
authoritative_sources: Subbarāma Dīkṣitar's Saṅgīta Sampradāya Pradarśinī (Vīṇā & Vocal Notation System)
The Ragas of Karnatic Music by N. S. Ramachandran (University of Madras, 1938)

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Tirupam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Quick deflection in 1/4 druta tempo, turning upon samvadi notes.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Sphuritam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Accented touch of the lower note in stepped pairs (1/3 druta tempo).

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Kampitam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Oscillation shaking the note at half a druta tempo.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Līnam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Soft merging of a note into its neighbor at druta speed.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Āndolitam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Heavy swinging oscillation held for laghu duration.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Vali
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Circling motion with irregular velocity like wind-blown waves.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Tribhinnam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Simultaneous touch traversing three sthayis continuously.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Kuruḷa
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Soft, knotty guttural turn resembling vali.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Āhatam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Striking the preceding note in ascending progression.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Ullāsitam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Ascending glide (zāru) sliding upwards through consecutive notes.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Plāvitam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Deep, wide oscillation sustained for pluta duration.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Humphitam / Gumphita
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Deep chest resonance producing the reverent sound of 'hum'.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Mudritam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Ornament produced with lips gently closed.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Nāmitam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Soft bending down of notes where tone is subtle and tender.

sangita_ratnakara_15.name: Miśritam
sangita_ratnakara_15.description: Artful combination or admixture of two or more gamakas.

mandra_sthayi.sensory_cue: Deep, warm, grounded resonance vibrating the sternum. Never push or shout.

madhya_sthayi.sensory_cue: Open throat like a gentle yawn, relaxed tongue blade, loose jaw. Pure baseline intonation.

tara_sthayi.sensory_cue: Light, ringing acoustic placement behind forehead and upper palate. Minimal breath pressure.

vowel_shaping_for_gamaka_clarity.pedagogical_use: Primary vowel for learning Kampitam oscillation and wide melodic arcs.

vowel_shaping_for_gamaka_clarity.jaw_position: Gentle smile, tongue high against molars
vowel_shaping_for_gamaka_clarity.pedagogical_use: Ideal for fast Sphuritam glottal accents and high-octave precision.

vowel_shaping_for_gamaka_clarity.jaw_position: Rounded oval lips, soft palate elevated
vowel_shaping_for_gamaka_clarity.pedagogical_use: Develops warm, ringing resonance in Mandra sthāyi slides (Jāru).

common_pronunciation_errors.symptom: Voice sounds choked; student shakes neck or jaw up and down to produce vibrato.
common_pronunciation_errors.corrective_drill: Sing on a relaxed sigh; use abdominal diaphragm pulses instead of jaw movements.

common_pronunciation_errors.symptom: Student sings rigid static pitches with zero life or microtonal curve.
common_pronunciation_errors.corrective_drill: Practice slow 2-note vocal slides (Jāru) before adding oscillations.

common_pronunciation_errors.symptom: When oscillating Gandhara, the pitch spills past Madhyama, distorting the rāga identity.
common_pronunciation_errors.corrective_drill: Use the visual pitch contour stencil to enforce strict upper-ceiling limits.

level_1_beginner.tier_name: Level 1: Beginner Foundation – The First Curves
level_1_beginner.target_audience: Children (Ages 6+), vocal beginners, and self-taught musicians starting Carnatic music.
level_1_beginner.core_objective: Transition from rigid, static pitch holding (Sthira Swara) into controlled, gentle microtonal curves and smooth slides without throat strain.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: The Gentle Swara Slide (Ullāsa Jāru)
exercises.description: Glide smoothly from Shadjam (S) up to Panchamam (P) on the open vowel 'Aa' without intermediate stepping.
exercises.pronunciation_cue: Start with relaxed belly breath on 'Sa', keep jaw still, glide continuous pitch like a violin string slide up to 'Pa'.

exercises.title: Exercise 2: The Descending River Slide (Iṟaṅga Jāru)
exercises.description: Glide downward from Panchamam (P) to Shadjam (S) on 'Aa' maintaining steady breath support.
exercises.pronunciation_cue: Never let the volume drop as pitch descends; keep chest resonance open as you land on 'Sa'.

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Slow Ocean Wave (Vilambita Kampitam)
exercises.description: Slow, relaxed oscillation on Antara Gandhara (G3) gently rocking between R1 (112 cents) and M1 (498 cents).
exercises.pronunciation_cue: Think of a swing or hammock. Do not vocalize 'ga-ga-ga'; produce one uninterrupted tone that rises and falls smoothly.

exercises.title: Exercise 4: The Janta Stepping Accent (Beginner Sphuritam)
exercises.sample_notation: S Sw  R Rw  G Gw
exercises.description: Sing paired notes from Janta Varisais, touching the lower neighbor note lightly on the second stroke.
exercises.pronunciation_cue: The first note is firm; the second note has a subtle diaphragmatic impulse that bounces from the note below.

game_meta.flight_theme: Stepping Stones in the Forest Temple

level_2_intermediate.tier_name: Level 2: Intermediate Classical Ornaments – The Daśavidha Repertoire
level_2_intermediate.target_audience: Students practicing Janta Varisais, Alankaras, and Gitams transitioning into Varnams.
level_2_intermediate.core_objective: Master the primary ornaments of the Daśavidha tradition: accurate speed doubling (Madhyama Kāla), downward flicks (Nōkku/Orika), and swinging arcs (Āndolitam).

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Classical Kampitam in Second Speed (Dvitīya Kāla)
exercises.description: Standard concert-speed oscillation at 4.5 Hz frequency across pure Suddha Madhyamam (498 cents).
exercises.pronunciation_cue: Oscillate evenly without trembling. Feel the rhythmic pulse of 4 full waves per beat of Ādi Tāla.

exercises.title: Exercise 2: The Downward Stress Flick (Nōkku)
exercises.description: Striking Gandhara with momentary pressure borrowed from Madhyama above, releasing immediately.
exercises.pronunciation_cue: Vocalize with sudden gentle stress from the upper note without sliding. Like tapping a drumhead.

exercises.title: Exercise 3: The Deflection Curve (Orika / Odigimpu)
exercises.description: As the note descends, the voice executes a momentary upward flick touching the higher note before resolving downwards.
exercises.pronunciation_cue: A graceful flip of the voice that catches the higher śruti for a split second on descent.

exercises.title: Exercise 4: The Pendulum Arc (Āndolitam)
exercises.description: Holding a note for 4 to 5 aksharas, then gently swinging outward to reveal the neighbor before returning.
exercises.pronunciation_cue: Sing like the heavy swing of a temple bell. Smooth, rounded pendulum curves with zero angularity.

level_3_expert.tier_name: Level 3: Advanced / Expert – Rāga-Specific Signature Embellishments
level_3_expert.target_audience: Advanced students, concert practitioners, and teachers mastering rāga bhāva.
level_3_expert.core_objective: Master rāga-defining microtonal oscillation boundaries, asymmetric vakra curves, and exact vibrational frequencies verified on sonometer acoustics.

exercises.title: Masterwork 1: The Plaintive Oscillation of Hanumatodi (Mela #8)
exercises.description: In Hanumatodi, Sadharana Gandhara (G2) is never sung as a flat static note; it continuously oscillates from R1 (288 Hz) up to M1 (345 Hz).
exercises.pronunciation_cue: Engage deep chest resonance. Begin oscillation from Suddha Rishabha and stretch the microtone upward without letting it touch static Western minor 3rd.

exercises.title: Masterwork 2: The Piercing Prati Madhyama Shake of Mechakalyāṇi (#65)
exercises.description: Sharp Prati Madhyamam (M2, 590 cents) oscillating intensely and dissolving directly into Panchamam (P, 702 cents).
exercises.pronunciation_cue: Sing with cranial mask resonance behind forehead. Keep the pitch razor-sharp and pull upward smoothly into Panchama.

exercises.title: Masterwork 3: The Signature Loop of Ānandabhairavi
exercises.ornament_type: Vakra Loop with Orika (S G2 R2 G2 M1 P)
exercises.notation_symbol: s g~ r g~ m p
exercises.description: The quintessential signature phrase of Ānandabhairavi weaving delicate oscillation on G2 around R2.
exercises.pronunciation_cue: Never articulate linear S-R-G; gracefully pivot the pitch around Rishabha with slight nasal resonance.

game_meta.flight_theme: The Sacred Temple Coil of Ānandabhairavi

exercises.title: Masterwork 4: The Regal Begada Madhyama Shake
exercises.description: The famous Begada Madhyama: starts below Suddha Madhyama, shakes with heavy oscillation reaching near Prati Madhyama.
exercises.pronunciation_cue: A bold, majestic shake. Hold firm breath pressure while letting the pitch cycle through its traditional Begada curve.

game_engine_overview.engine_name: Nāda Vāhana 2D Canvas Game Loop Engine

canvas_coordinate_mapping.x_axis: Time in milliseconds mapped horizontally from left (t = 0) to right (t = exercise_duration_ms). Viewport scrolls smoothly at constant speed matching the Tala tempo.
canvas_coordinate_mapping.y_axis: Pitch in microtonal cents (0 to 1200 cents relative to user's selected Kattai tonic S). Bottom = Mandra Sthāyi, Middle = Madhya Sthāyi, Top = Tāra Sthāyi.

kid_friendly_flight_mechanics.concept: The student's voice acts as an aerodynamic flight controller. Steady singing levitates the character; microtonal oscillations pilot the avatar through colorful mountain passes, river waves, and cosmic star corridors.
kid_friendly_flight_mechanics.smoothing_filter: Linear interpolation (LERP factor 0.18) on detected microphone frequency prevents jitter and sudden jumps while preserving authentic gamaka speed.
kid_friendly_flight_mechanics.star_collection_system: Golden musical stars are suspended along the ideal classical trajectory. Holding pitch within the tolerance ribbon magnetically collects stars, emitting joyful chimes and sparkling particle bursts.
kid_friendly_flight_mechanics.combo_multiplier: Staying on-pitch for consecutive beats builds up a 'Nāda Combo' (1.0x -> 1.5x -> 2.0x -> 3.0x), rewarding sustained vocal control.

three_interactive_game_modes.name: Nāda Vāhana (Voice Pilot Stencil Flight)
three_interactive_game_modes.description: Piloting the vocal avatar along the continuous Gamaka ribbon. Fly through Ullāsa Jāru slides, Kampitam waves, and Sphuritam peaks, collecting stars and dodging ceiling overshoots.
hud_elements: Real-time score & combo multiplier (x1.0, x1.5, x2.0, x3.0)
Star counter (0 to 3 stars per exercise)
Microtonal deviation gauge (± cents from target)
Current Swarasthana indicator (S, R1, G3, M1, P, D1, N3, Ṡ)

win_conditions.gold_star: Score >= 90% with 0 boundary overshoots and 80%+ star collection

three_interactive_game_modes.name: Śruti Arcade (Svara Match & Catch)
three_interactive_game_modes.description: The engine plays an authentic 22-Śruti microtone or an embellished gamaka phrase. The student has 3 seconds to reproduce the exact pitch or identify the swara by singing it, catching floating lotus pearls.
hud_elements: Target sound replay button (Hear Tambura reference)
Accuracy meter (Exact microtone vs close semitone)

win_conditions.silver_star: 10 consecutive correct catches with <= 15 cents deviation
win_conditions.gold_star: 15 consecutive catches at concert tolerance (<= 10 cents deviation)

three_interactive_game_modes.name: Laya Taraṅga (Tāla Wave Surfer)
three_interactive_game_modes.description: Surfing the gamaka wave in sync with the Tāla beat. Synchronizes the 4.8 Hz Kampitam oscillations with the clapping hand kriyās of Ādi and Rūpaka tālas.
hud_elements: Animated Tala Kriyā indicator (Taṭṭu, Vīccu, Finger counts)
Wave sync pulse (glowing ripple on every akshara beat)
Rhythm tightness gauge (Too fast / Perfect Laya / Dragging)

win_conditions.bronze_star: Complete 1 full avartana with smooth continuous oscillation
win_conditions.gold_star: Complete 4 avartanas across 1x and 2x speeds without breaking rhythm

realtime_audio_input_and_pitch_tracker.algorithm: Hybrid YIN / McLeod Pitch Method (MPM) with Lookahead Parabolic Interpolation

octave_jump_guard.fallback_strategy: Clamp to previous stable pitch if sudden 2x jump lacks physical glide trajectory

realtime_evaluation_and_scoring_engine.algorithm_name: Dynamic Time Warping Contour & Boundary Matcher (DTW-CBM) with Dual-Lens Telemetry

child_view.primary_display: Stars (1 to 3 Stars), Golden Musical Notes, Flying Combos, and Joyful Fanfare
child_view.feedback_tone: Encouraging, game-like, celebration of steady voice control without anxiety-inducing microtonal technicalities.

guru_parent_view.primary_display: Cents RMS Deviation (e.g. ±8.4c), DTW Contour Distance, Boundary Ceiling Overshoots (0 to N), and Gamaka Suddham %
guru_parent_view.feedback_tone: Rigorous, musicologically authentic, traceable directly to the 22-Śruti harmonic matrix and classical treatises.
